newsitem.title: JAPAN: ASIAN CRUDE OIL ADRIFT IN BEACONLESS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN CRUDE OIL ADRIFT IN BEACONLESS MARKET.

text.p: Crude prices were still in Asia on Monday, with physical trade slack, SIMEX Brent crude unquoted, and spot acquisitions for October Persian Gulf (PG) grades still a week away, traders said.
Even news of a partial refinery shutdown in Japan over the next ten days, and the spectre of Iraqi barrels headed eastward failed to offer direction to the markets.
Brokers pegged notional September Brent values at $18.55/18.65 at 0615 GMT, unchanged from morning levels, and in line with the Monday IPE close of $18.58.
A bona fide start to October trading of PG grades was predicted by traders to experience delays due to uncertainty surrounding the volumes of Iraqi crude headed into Asia.
"There will be nervousness until we know exactly how much Iraqi grade is going to hit the region," said one trader.
"Much of the price volatility expected from the resumption of exports has already been played out," said a trader with a Japanese refiner.
"But buyers in Japan still have no idea what they can or cannot expect from Iraq, so they are likely to wait as long as they can before committing themselves to other grades," he said.
"We are still having our doubts," he added.
Japan traders mainly shrugged off the closure of a 150,000 barrel per day topping unit in central Japan in light of already lacklustre domestic demand and ample product inventories.
The topper at Showa Yokkaichi, in central Japan, was hit by a fire on Monday and is likely to remain closed for at least 10 days as authorities review safety measures at the facility.
Showa Yokkaichi, which belongs to the Showa Shell Sekiyu KK group, will compensate for the expected loss in production by securing oil products from other group refineries.
"The timing of this accident is not such that it will have a significant market impact," said one trader.
"If anything, it may dampen the call on Malaysian crude, but the plant takes no Indonesian," a regional crude trader with a Japan trading company said.
Traders said they were expecting news on bids for Malaysia's September Bunga Kekwa crude tender sometime Tuesday evening, following the 0700 GMT deadline.
The tender is offering 250,000 barrels of crude, loading between September 9-14. --P.Lardner/Tokyo Energy Desk- 813-5473-3708
